tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description begins with imperative instruction ('Use when a user asks to review, audit, assess, or health-check...'), focuses on user intent/triggers rather than internal implementation, explicitly lists trigger phrases and scenarios (including the case where the user doesn't name resources), and remains a tight paragraph despite being information-dense.
tests.evidence: Use when a user asks to review, audit, assess, or health-check FSx for NetApp ONTAP (FSxN / FSx ONTAP) ... Activate even on a brief request with no file-system IDs ... Triggers: "FSxN operational review", "FSx ONTAP review", "review my FSxN", "audit my FSx ONTAP"...

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body is dense but almost entirely domain-specific — pillar/check listings, API quirks, severity/evidence rules, and FSxN-specific procedures. It does not explain generic concepts the agent already knows; everything is non-obvious operational detail specific to this review.
tests.evidence: This is a strict READ-ONLY, fully automated review. Every check is driven by a public AWS Describe*/List*/Get* call or a CloudWatch metric read.

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: The body summarizes pillars/checks in a compact table and defers the detailed thresholds/logic/severities to per-pillar reference files, rather than embedding the actual check definitions inline.
tests.evidence: The check definitions are split across small reference files for reliable loading: ... Load references/overview.md first ... Then load the per-pillar checks file for each pillar you run

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: All six reference files are linked via markdown links in the body.

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each reference link specifies when to load it (first, at start of pillar's checks, as authoritative API/logic source).
tests.evidence: Then load the per-pillar checks file for each pillar you run — load it when you start that pillar's checks

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference links use relative paths rooted at references/.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile, consistency-critical operations (evidence rules, severity assignment, pagination, read-only constraints) are given exact prescriptive instructions, while report framing retains some flexibility (e.g., 'summarize passing checks in aggregate').
tests.evidence: Read-only. Describe*/List*/Get* only; paginate every token. No Create*/Update*/Delete*, no data-plane access, no mounting, no ONTAP CLI.

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: The skill does not present competing tools as equal options; it specifies the exact AWS APIs to use (fsx, cloudwatch, backup, ec2) with no alternative tooling suggested.
tests.evidence: Public AWS APIs only, via `use_aws`: `fsx` (...), `cloudwatch` (...), `backup` (...), and `ec2` (...). No ONTAP CLI, no data-plane calls, no non-AWS tooling

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The skill teaches a generalizable procedure (discover scope, run checks per pillar, validate, report) that applies to any FSxN account/region/file-system, not a one-off instance.
tests.evidence: Step 1 — Identify scope. Default path (no clarification round-trip): if the user gives no specifics, default to the current account/region via sts:GetCallerIdentity, discover all ONTAP file systems...

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: A dedicated Gotchas section lists concrete, specific, non-obvious corrections (Gen2 metric absence, latency unit conversion, idle system behavior, thin-provisioning).
tests.evidence: Gen2 file systems do not emit `StorageCapacityUtilization`. ... Latency metrics are in seconds. `DataReadOperationTime ÷ DataReadOperations`... multiply by 1000 and label ms.

tests.name: Templates and outputs missing
tests.reasoning: The skill provides a report template in assets/ referenced for the full tabular report case, and inline minimal output requirements for the chat case.
tests.evidence: load `assets/report-template.md` and render the complete layout — H1 title, the account/region/date header, the AI Disclaimer blockquote verbatim...

tests.name: Templates and outputs must not be in body
tests.reasoning: The body only lists minimum required report elements as bullet points, not a full inline template; the actual large template lives in assets/report-template.md.
tests.evidence: The response MUST contain, at minimum: 1. a title line identifying it as an FSx for NetApp ONTAP operational review... 4. a short 'healthy / not evaluated' note

tests.name: Asset files must be linked
tests.reasoning: The single asset file report-template.md is referenced in the body.
tests.evidence: load `assets/report-template.md` and render the complete layout

tests.name: Asset links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: The asset reference specifies the condition under which to load it (full tabular report / Evaluation agent / explicit user request).
tests.evidence: Full tabular report (Evaluation agent, or when the user explicitly asks for the "full report"): load `assets/report-template.md` and render the complete layout

tests.name: Asset path format
tests.reasoning: The asset reference uses a relative path from skill root.

tests.name: Step-by-step guidance
tests.reasoning: The ordered, dependent procedure is presented as a checkbox checklist with 'Step N' labels, and nested sub-items also use checkboxes.
tests.evidence: - [ ] **Step 1 — Identify scope.** ... - [ ] **Step 2 — Run the checks.** ... - [ ] **Step 3 — Validate your own output, then generate the report.**

tests.name: Validation loops
tests.reasoning: Step 3 is an explicit self-validation step instructing the agent to check its own output for errors (citations, severity reconciliation, exact IDs, no invented numbers) before presenting.
tests.evidence: Step 3 — Validate your own output, then generate the report. First self-check and fix any problem before presenting: ... Severity counts reconcile ... No invented numbers, no ONTAP CLI, no manual steps anywhere in the report.
